memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You are to lay your hand on the head of your offering and slaughter it at the entrance to the tent of meeting. Then Aaron's sons the priests shall splash the blood against the sides of the altar.'" - Lev 3:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Even the celebration offering begins with a hand on a head and blood on an altar.

That is worth pausing over. This was the happiest of the sacrifices — the one that ended in feasting. And yet God did not allow it to skip the blood. There is no fellowship with a holy God that bypasses the cost of dealing with sin.

We live in a time when people are eager for the fellowship part without the blood part. They want God's comfort, God's peace, God's presence at the table — but without the cross, without repentance, without the uncomfortable truth that sin required a death. Leviticus will not permit it. The route to the feast runs past the altar.

Paul says it directly: you who once were far away have been brought near by the blood of Christ (Eph 2:13). And again: God was pleased to reconcile to himself all things by making peace through his blood, shed on the cross (Col 1:20). Our peace was not declared. It was purchased.

So when you come to God freely and gladly — and you should come gladly — remember what made the freedom possible. Every meal at God's table was bought at an altar.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I want the comfort of God's presence without reckoning with the cost of the cross?
2. How does remembering the price of my peace change the way I approach God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, my peace with the Father cost You everything. Let me never take my welcome at Your table lightly. Amen.
